html:
Merengue is the national music and dance of the Dominican Republic. It took shape in the 19th century in the Cibao valley around Santiago, played on accordion, the tambora drum and the guira scraper.

Elites first scorned it as rural and African. Rafael Trujillo, who came from a humble background, made it the national music in the 1930s, and bands played songs in his praise.

From the 1980s fast, brassy merengue spread through Latin America and to New York, and singers such as Juan Luis Guerra won fame worldwide. UNESCO listed merengue in 2016. It shaped the compas of Haiti, and it now shares Dominican dance floors with bachata.
